**Finding submitted — INDEMN: deviation (fallback redline validated).**

- **What the document does:** Section 12.1.1 (p0687–p0691) lists SFJ's indemnity heads — gross negligence/wilful misconduct, material breach, Protocol breach, AZ License breach, post-transfer injury and product liability — with **no third-party IP infringement head anywhere** in the Agreement (searches for IP-infringement indemnity language returned nothing outside Article 12). Section 12.1.2(f) (p0695) runs the *only* IP indemnity in the wrong direction: PB indemnifies SFJ for infringement "by the Product **or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder**" — i.e. we cover SFJ's own infringing performance. That is the rule's walk-away scenario.
- **Already adequate, left untouched:** the 12.2 procedure (notice p0698, control of defence p0699, cooperation p0705) and the mutual gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct coverage.
- **Target level:** fallback. The preferred position would require striking the negotiated subject-injury and product-liability heads in 12.1.2(b)–(g) — a collateral rewrite. The fallback checklist is met by one inserted paragraph inside 12.1.1 (so the existing 12.2 procedure applies without a dangling cross-reference) carrying the IP indemnity, the PB modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace, refund, and the 3× super-cap scoped to that new indemnity only (there is no existing liability cap, so it is not extended to SFJ's other indemnities).
- **Conforming cut:** 12.1.2(f) is trimmed to infringement by the Product only, so the retained PB indemnity no longer contradicts the new SFJ indemnity; all other words of (f) and the surrounding heads are preserved verbatim.
